arn_001: You can recognise them by three sweet chestnut trunks at the castle gate, the two heavy ones side by side at 750 and 718 centimetres round and a leaner third at 472. They stand either side of the path into Kasteel Zijpendaal.
arn_002: You can recognise it by the crown, 35 metres across, and a trunk about 6.2 metres round, with a beech and self-seeded Douglas firs crowding it for light. It stands above the path that climbs from Dalweg to Braamweg.
arn_003: You can recognise it by the short stem and arms so thick they read as separate trunks, about 7.1 to 7.5 metres round. It stands where the Huissensedijk meets the small white Bonifatiuskerk in Elden.
arn_006: You can recognise it by branches trained to cascade rather than reach, with white flowers hanging at shoulder height in summer. It stands on the roadside edge of Velperplein, directly in front of Musis Sacrum.
arn_008: You can recognise it by the conspicuous wound low on the trunk and the cavity above it, on a black walnut whose crown has thinned since the 1990s. It stands in the green strip on the northwest side of Velperplein.
arn_009: You can recognise it by the acorns, on short stalks pressed close to the twig rather than dangling. It stands in Musispark along Eusebiusbuitensingel near Parkstraat, about 65 metres from the old Canadian poplar.
arn_010: You can recognise it by a crown that went sideways rather than upward, because it has had open room around it from the start. It stands beside the 1931 Lorentz Monument in Park Sonsbeek.
arn_011: You can recognise it as the old oak the park's own monumental tree route stops at. It stands beside the Witte Watermolen, the white watermill on the Sint Jansbeek in Park Sonsbeek.
arn_012: You can recognise it by deadwood through the crown and weak regrowth, one of three heavy oaks standing together. It stands at the woodland edge on the northeast side of the Sonsbeek meadow, where the grass runs out.
arn_013: You can recognise it by branches gone out rather than up, an oak grown alone with nothing competing for its light. It stands in a grazed meadow, often closed off with electric wire, at the corner of Zijpendaalseweg and Sonsbeekweg.
